title: Justifying faith includes historical virtue — as rational soul includes lower life
source_text: XIX. Hinc quoque liquet, ex Reformatorum mente, fidem justificantem ita diversam esse a fide historica, ut omnem ejus virtutem includat; atque sic ab ea distingui, ut perfectum ab imperfecto, sive ea distinctione qua gradus superior ab inferiori differt. Etenim fides justificans ad fidem mortuam atque historicam se habet quemadmodum anima rationalis ad sensitivam & vegetativam, quarum vim & facultates, vitam, sensum, & motum eminenter complectitur, & gradum rationis addit. Nam sic quoque fides justificans facit ut omnia credamus quae verbo Dei docentur, quod praestat fides historica. Sed supra illam habet, quod mentem Theoreticam luculentius irradiat, practicam vero potenter afficit & alte penetrat; & acriorem veritatis sensum, assensumque firmiorem animis nostris ingignit, quam fides ista iners & otiosa. Tum etiam quaecunque ex verbo Dei hausit, ad actionem refert, vitamque instituendam, & credenti cuique sigillatim certa quadam ratione applicat.
pass_a_gloss: Hence also it is clear, according to the mind of the Reformers, that justifying faith is so diverse from historical faith that it includes all its virtue; and is so distinguished from it as the perfect from the imperfect, or by that distinction by which a superior degree differs from an inferior. For justifying faith stands to dead and historical faith as the rational soul stands to the sensitive and vegetative, whose force and faculties — life, sense, and motion — it eminently embraces, and adds the degree of reason. For so also justifying faith makes us believe all things which are taught by the word of God, which historical faith accomplishes. But above that it has this: that it irradiates the Theoretical mind more brightly, but powerfully affects and deeply penetrates the practical, and engenders a sharper sense of truth and firmer assent in our minds than that idle and otiose faith. Then also whatever it has drawn from the word of God it refers to action and to ordering life, and applies to each believer individually in a certain definite way.
pass_b_english: Justifying faith differs from historical yet includes all its virtue — perfect vs imperfect; higher degree.
Analogy: rational soul to sensitive/vegetative — embraces lower powers and adds reason.
It also believes all God teaches (as historical faith does).
Above that: brighter theoretical light, deeper practical penetration, sharper sense, firmer assent; refers revelation to life and applies it personally.
